title: GPU fluctuation patterns and noise-floor analysis (working)
content:
Summary:

This is a working analysis of short-duration performance/health fluctuations observed across a subset of our GPU fleet (clusters: us-west-2-a, us-west-2-c, dev-gpu-pool). Unlike large, persistent failures (hard ECC storms or deterministic kernel panics), these events are: intermittent, low-amplitude in telemetry (spikes in correctable ECC + small nvlink link error counters), and frequently precede brief driver reinitializations or process eviction within 30–90s. The pattern shows up in P95 latency jitter on small requests and a subtle uptick in transient CUDA context loss traces.

Goal:
- Characterize the "noise-floor" events (short, noisy bursts) and separate them from full-blown instability incidents.
- Produce quick mitigations that reduce customer-visible impact without heavy-handed evictions.
- Define a reproducible experiment matrix and telemetry dashboard slices to detect precursors.

Observed signals (raw):
- Correctable ECC spikes (per-GPU) that last 5–45s, count delta 5–40 per minute during bursts.
- NVLink lane error counters step up by small integers with asymmetric distribution between peers.
- Driver logs show transient GPU watchdog messages, followed by a single "device lost" or driver module reload ~10% of the time.
- Kubernetes kubelet eviction events correlated to slightly elevated cgroup CPU wait time and short-lived memory reclaim activity.
- No immediate PSU or ambient thermal alarms in the systems that exhibit the smallest amplitude bursts.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Link negotiation micro-retries: NVLink fabric sometimes re-trains for short intervals under certain memory access patterns (heavy small batch KV cache loads), causing correctable error counters and occasional brief stalls.
2) Kernel/driver jitter under contended ISR path: a pathological interrupt storm on BDF path causes transient scheduler delays that look like small context timeouts.
3) Aging DIMM/controller interaction causing momentary refresh pressure visible as correctables but not as machine-level logs.
4) Environmental EMI/noise affecting PCIe/NVLink signaling on specific racks (less likely but plausible for adjacent node correlation).

Immediate mitigations (low blast radius):
- Adjust per-pool eviction threshold window from 120s -> 90s for nodes with frequent micro-bursts to prefer soft-evict (restart container) over full node quarantine. Owner: Arjun. ETA: 48h to roll config.
- Enable temporary increased sampling of per-GPU ECC counters (1s resolution vs 10s) for candidate nodes and route to the new telemetry topic gpu-noise-floor. Owner: Sofia. ETA: 24h.
- Add lightweight request-level retry at the edge (two attempts with exponential backoff) for small gen requests (<1k tokens) routed to dev-gpu-pool. Owner: Platform SDK. ETA: 72h.

Experiment plan (reproducibility):
- Controlled load generator: run a traffic profile that mimics KV cache heavy access (many short sequences, random prefixes) against a set of repro nodes and a control set. Measurement axes: ECC per-second, NVLink lane flips, driver warnings, P50/P95 latencies. Owner: Ben. Start: 2029-08-15.
- A/B kernel driver: deploy driver variant A (stock) vs B (tuned IRQ coalescing) across matched hardware. Measure ISR counts and user-visible stalls. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/342.
- Synthetic EMI test: schedule a maintenance window to reposition suspect nodes' neighbor blades and run identical loads to see adjacency correlation. Not urgent; tentative Q4.

Telemetry: dashboards and alerts to build
- gpu-noise-floor overview: per-cluster heatmap showing short bursts (events per hour with duration <60s).
- precursor detector: rolling-window (5 min) of correctable ECC rate + nvlink delta; fire a low-severity PagerDuty alert (SLO: <2 pagers/week) when spike pattern matches template.
- eviction trace correlate: join kubelet evictions to GPU transient flags within a 2-minute window (to avoid attributing unrelated evictions).

Runbook snippets (quick reference for oncall):
- If you see a P95 latency spike that coincides with short ECC burst and no thermal/PSU alarms: 1) move traffic away from the node by scaling down the route to 0 and re-route to Dedicated fallback; 2) increase ECC sampling for 30 minutes and attach logs to Jira SRE-1284; 3) run "gpu-check-firmware" script and note firmware revisions.
- If driver module reload observed: capture dmesg, kernel oops, and full driver logs, then taint node (soft quarantine) and open a debug session with the serving-runtime team.

Data snapshot (example):
- Node gpu-uw2-a-12: 2029-08-11 03:12–03:14 UTC: ECC correctables rose by 28 within 90s; nvlink-peer-2 reported 3 lane errors; process eviction of container rtx-service-7 occurred at 03:13:37; driver reported "minor interrupt latency" (trace id: tf-cc-77). No PSU/thermal alerts.

Ownership and next steps:
- Arjun: rollout eviction-window config change to staging pools. (Due 2029-08-14).
- Sofia: implement gpu-noise-floor topic and 1s ECC sampling for candidate nodes; prepare dashboard tiles. (Due 2029-08-13).
- Ben: start controlled load generator runs and draft experiment README. (Start 2029-08-15).
- Maya: schedule cross-team sync (serving-runtime, infra, telemetry) for 2029-08-16 to review A/B and preliminary data.

Unresolved questions / decision points:
- Tolerance: how many short bursts per hour should route-level fallback trigger? Need product guidance to weigh cost vs availability.
- Long-term: do we prefer kernel-level IRQ tuning across the fleet or selective NVLink firmware updates? Cost and risk analysis needed.

Attachments / links:
- Quick log query examples and saved queries inserted in the linked artifacts.
- Note: CONFLUENCE-6392 contains prior NVLink training hypothesis drafts; link for long-context history.

Appendix: quick log grep snippets for oncall
- ECC spikes: "resource.type=machine AND metric.name=GPU_ECC_CORRECTABLE AND metric.delta>5 AND duration<=60s"
- NVLink peer flip: "nvlink.*lane_error.*peer=.*"

Free-format notes / rough ideas (scratchpad):
- Could try a very short adaptive micro-restart (stop container for 5s then resume) when we detect these micro-bursts to avoid wasting a node quarantine; risky but low resource cost.
- Consider adding a per-node rolling baseline (last-24h median + MAD) so we detect deviations relative to the node's historical noise floor instead of fleet-wide static thresholds.

Status: draft; will update after early telemetry runs and the 2029-08-15 experiments.
